notes: J0927−6335: Included as a follow-up of a previously identified Galactic hypervelocity star. At T:p1-b9 the authors call it the "fastest known Galactic hypervelocity star" with a space velocity of about 2800 km/s; at T:p1-b12 they identify it as one of the objects found by El-Badry et al. (2023); and at T:p1-b13 they describe this paper's HST observation. The paper does not literally use "unbound" or give an explicit escape-speed comparison, so inclusion relies on the established meaning of "Galactic hypervelocity star" plus the reported speed, not on the "runaway" or D6 designation alone.

J0927−6335: The paper reports a total “space velocity” of ≈2800 km/s for this Galactic hypervelocity star (T:p1-b9, T:p1-b12), but does not explicitly name the reference frame; under the standard hypervelocity-star interpretation I record it as the Galactic rest-frame total speed. No equatorial coordinates, parallax or distance, proper motions, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported in the supplied material.
